remediation_steps.step:
Back up the source file before making any edits.

Command:
    cp /opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py /opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

Why: Backing up the file ensures that you can restore the original state if the changes introduce any issues.

Replace the use of pickle.loads with json.loads to safely deserialize the data.

Command:
  #EDIT_FILE
  {"path": "/opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py",
   "old_text": "data = pickle.loads(decoded)",
   "new_text": "data = json.loads(decoded)"}

Why: Using json.loads instead of pickle.loads prevents arbitrary code execution as JSON does not support object serialization.

Verify that the vulnerable pattern is no longer present in the file.

Command:
  #VERIFY_ABSENT
  {"path": "/opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py",
   "pattern": "pickle.loads"}

Why: Ensuring the absence of the vulnerable pattern confirms that the insecure deserialization has been removed.

Run a syntax check to ensure the edited file is still valid Python code.

Command:
    python3 -m py_compile /opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py

Why: Syntax checking ensures that the file is free of syntax errors after the edit.

issue.title: Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on user-supplied Lambda event data. Use json.loads or a safe format.
